title: Austin's Audit, Auto Fines & Iron Sheds
summary:
*   **Financial Oversight:** A new "Auditorium Account" was established to accurately track all income and expenses related to the city's auditorium building.
*   **Traffic Fine Remissions:** Two $19.80 fines were forgiven, including one for a non-resident who was unfamiliar with local automobile speed limits.
*   **Fire & Police Force Updates:** New rules were adopted for paid employees of the Colorado Hose Company No. 2, and a new patrolman was appointed.
*   **Downtown Development:** A revocable permit was granted to the General Manager of the Austin American newspaper to erect an all-iron shed behind their Congress Avenue office.

772
Regular meeting of the City Council : Austin, Texas, April 30, 1914

The Council was called to order by the Mayor : Roll called : Present Mayor Wooldridge,
Councilmen Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes & Powell 5 Absent none.
The minutes of the last regular meeting were read and adopted:

Councilman Anthony presented bids for painting roofs & Tower of Colorado Fire Hall as
follows:
Walter J Daly $ 105.00
Tony Wagner 72.05
C G Saladee 125.00.
On motion of Councilman Anthony, the contract for the said work, was awarded to Tony
Wagner , for $ 72.05, by the following vote: Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen Anthony,
Bartholomew, Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.

The Mayor laid before the Council the following resolution : Whereas, from time to time
there are receipts of money from the rental of the auditorium Building in this City,
situated upon the Public Park lying between Guadalupe and San Antonio streets , and
expenditures of money be reason of the maintenance of the auditorium located on the above
described property;and Whereas, at the present time there is no specificate account kept
by either the Assessor & collector nor the City Treasurorof the receipts and expenditures
of said auditorium Building.
Now, therefore,
Resolved by the City Council of the City of Austin; Texas: That both the Assessor &
collector and the City Treasurer of the City of Austin, Texas, are authorized and
instructed to open anappropriate account , entitled " Auditorium Account " , in which the
receipts and expenditures of money by reason of the maintenance and conduct of said
auditorium shall be correctly entered.
The resolution was adopted by the following vote : Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.
Councilman Anthony offered the following resolution : Resolved by the City Council of the
City of Austin: That, in consideration of the fact that R R Banner was and is a
non-resident of Austin and not familiar with its automobile speed limits law s, the fine
of $ 19.80 imposed upon him on April 8th 1914, in cause No 8470 in the Corporation Court
of the City of Austin, Texas, be and the same is hereby remitted .
The resolution was adopted by the following vote: Yeas mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.

Approved, A P Wooldridge, Mayor.

May 5th 1914.
The Council was called to order by the Mayor with all members present: The Mayor laid
before the Council the following resolution : Be it resolved by the City Council of the
City of Austin,Texas: That theCity Treasurer be and he is hereby instructed to transfer
the sum of five thousand,seventy three & 12/100 ($ 5073.12),from the General Street
Improve-ment fundto the Sanitary Sewer Earnings fundfor the purpose of re- imbursing said
fund for the $ 5.000.00 borrowed from saod fund by the General Street Improvement fund on
November 1st, 1913, together with interest at the rate of 3.51per cent for five months.
The resolution was adopted by the following vote: Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen
Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes & Powell 5 Nays none.
The Mayor laid before the Council the following resolution : Resolved by the City Council
of the City of Austin : That a permit be and is hereby granted to A G Smoot, General
Manager of the Austin American ,to erect and maintain a galvanized Iron Shed ,eight feet
by thirty feet , in the rear of the building located at 813 Congress Avenue in this City.
No part of this structure ,either in the upright posts,or roof joists,or otherwise, is to
be of wood,the whole structure is to be of Iron.
Be it further resolved by the City Council of the City of Austin : That this permit is
revocable at any time in the pleasure of the City Council The resolution was adopted by
the following vote : Yeas Mayor Wooldridge, Councilmen Anthony, Bartholomew, Haynes &
Powell 5 Nays none.
Approved, A P Wooldridge, Mayor.
The Council then adjourned.
